newsitem.title: HUNGARY: FORECAST-Hungary jobless rate seen flat in H1 '97.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Hungary jobless rate seen flat in H1 '97.

text.p: Unemployment in Hungary will not increase beyond its current level of 480,000 to 490,000, or 10.6 percent, in the first half of 1997, officials said on Tuesday.

"The number of workplaces -- which has seen a reduction of 1.4 million since the regime change (in 1990) -- will stop shrinking and this is encouraging," Labour Minister Peter Kiss told a news conference.
He added the government will spend 23.4 billion forints on unemployment benefit and job creation programmes next year and an additional four billion forints on public works. @

Judit Szekely, director of the National Labour Centre (OMK) said that while the total number of jobless remains unchanged the official figure could fall by some tens of thousands next year due to changing regulations.
"Tens of thousands of people will probably not meet new criteria, thus would no longer appear in our statistics."

She added that according to a recent OMK survey they expect a marginal increase in company output and therefore some job creation next year as a result of increased economic growth and domestic consumption.
She also said that business leaders are slightly more optimistic about the overall state of Hungary's economy than they were in the first half of 1996. @
"The proportion of those who say the economy is in a bad shape was 63.7 percent in the second half of 1996 compared with 69.2 percent in the first half of the year.
She added an insignificant percentage of those polled said the economy was in good shape, with the rest judging it as mediocre.
